Sepsis-3 is a clinical definition, not an ICD code. rendehR ships one
implementation per source family so the same rule runs on MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV
and eICU, with the source-specific tables and item IDs each database needs.

## The definition

The Third International Consensus defines sepsis as suspected infection
co-occurring with an acute increase in organ dysfunction, measured by the SOFA
score. The packaged implementation follows the widely used operational form:

1. **Suspected infection.** Pair an antibiotic with a body-fluid culture. If
   the culture came first, the antibiotic must follow within 72 hours; if the
   antibiotic came first, the culture must follow within 24 hours. The earlier
   event of the first qualifying pair is the suspicion time.
2. **SOFA.** Compute the six-organ SOFA score over the stay and keep windows
   with **SOFA ≥ 2 in absolute terms**.
3. **Combination.** Keep ICU stays where a qualifying SOFA window falls within
   −48 to +24 hours of the suspicion time.

The 72-hour and 24-hour windows point in opposite directions on purpose: a
culture drawn first can be followed by antibiotics for up to 72 hours, while an
antibiotic given first must be paired with a culture within 24 hours.

eICU has no culture table equivalent to MIMIC's, so its implementation uses
antibiotic-only suspicion (the ricu convention) and its own SOFA port. The
MIMIC-III implementation includes the SOFA port as well, so the absolute
SOFA ≥ 2 rule applies on every source, not only the one it was written for.

## Using the helper


``` r
ehr_init_project(
  "mimic_iv_demo", base_dir = "sepsis-demo",
  raw_data_root = normalizePath("rendehr-demo/data/source_data")
)
```



`build_sepsis_cohort()` runs the packaged SQL and returns the selected
identifiers. With `import = FALSE` it writes only a CSV, so you can inspect the
cohort before committing it to a project:


``` r
out <- file.path(docs_root, "sepsis-demo/mimic_iv_demo_sepsis3.csv")
build_sepsis_cohort(
  "mimic_iv_demo", bundle = "sepsis3",
  import = FALSE, out_csv = out, show_progress = FALSE
)
ids <- read.csv(out)
nrow(ids)
#> [1] 62
length(unique(ids$subject_id))
#> [1] 47
head(ids)
#>   subject_id  stay_id
#> 1   10007818 32359580
#> 2   10004720 35009126
#> 3   10020740 35044342
#> 4   10002428 38875437
#> 5   10037975 39061571
#> 6   10005817 31316840
```

The result carries the ICU stay and its patient (`stay_id`, `subject_id`),
matching the unit the definition selects. The same call with `import = TRUE` (the default) imports
the cohort and its context into the project; `import_scope = "hospital"` is the
default because a sepsis stay is usually analysed with its admission.

## Four variants

| Bundle | Selection |
|:--|:--|
| `sepsis3` | Every qualifying ICU stay |
| `first_sepsis3` | The patient's first-ever ICU stay, if it qualifies |
| `sepsis3_admission` | Qualifying suspicion within ±1 day of ICU admission |
| `first_sepsis3_admission` | Both restrictions |

`first_sepsis3` is the patient's first ICU stay, not the first septic stay, and
the eICU ordering of stays across hospitalisations is approximate. The four
bundles exist because published studies differ on the eligibility window and on
whether only the first stay counts; choosing one explicitly is better than
silently inheriting another study's choice.

## Counts on the demos

The bundled SQL was run on all three open demos. The numbers below are ICU
stays / hospital admissions / patients, where the source has an admission
identifier:

| Bundle | MIMIC-IV demo | MIMIC-III demo | eICU demo |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `sepsis3` | 62 / — / 47 | 95 / 92 / 70 | 448 / 429 / 389 |
| `first_sepsis3` | 40 / — / 40 | 66 / 66 / 66 | 353 / 353 / 353 |
| `sepsis3_admission` | 59 / — / 45 | 88 / 86 / 66 | 347 / 341 / 311 |
| `first_sepsis3_admission` | 39 / — / 39 | 61 / 61 / 61 | 283 / 283 / 283 |

The eICU suspicion-only cohort (no SOFA confirmation) is larger: 582 ICU stays
in 544 admissions and 489 patients. On MIMIC-III the suspicion-only cohort has
28 stays, and the modified suspicion implementation 109 stays in 102 admissions
and 78 patients. These are the same definitions the validation compares against
ricu, not a separate implementation.

## A second implementation in the concept layer

The `ehr` concept layer also contains the MIT-LCP `sepsis3` SQL, adapted so it
can read rendehR's harmonized tables. It is a concept, not a cohort: use it to
compare the packaged cohort with the upstream definition, or to study its
intermediate tables (SOFA, suspicion). For cohort selection, use
`build_sepsis_cohort()`; for the clinical concepts behind it, use
`run_concepts(layers = "ehr")`.
